tool.name: KeyedDatasetDiff
tool.summary: Compares an old and a new version of a feature class or table by one or more key fields and lists, per key, which rows were added or deleted, which attributes changed (old and new value) and how far the geometry moved. Duplicate keys are reported instead of being mis-matched. Read-only.

param.name: old_data
param.dialogReference: The earlier version (feature layer, feature class or table).

param.name: new_data
param.dialogReference: The later version, with the same key fields.

param.name: key_fields
param.dialogReference: One or more fields of the old data that identify a row. Each is found in the new data in this order: a field with exactly the same name (then the same name ignoring case); else a field whose alias matches the name, then a field whose name matches it, both ignoring case, spaces, dashes and underscores; else the same two checks with the old field's alias. If a key field is numeric on one side and text on the other, keys are compared by their text form (a DATE at 00:00:00 is written as the ISO date only, so it matches the text 2024-01-05; a text holding an ISO date and time, such as 2024-01-05 00:00:00, is read as that date and time, so it matches too; spaces around such a text are ignored). A date and time with a UTC offset (TIMESTAMPOFFSET) is matched by the instant it stands for, as for attributes; it never matches a DATE or DATEONLY key (no offset), and the run warns when the key field has one of these types on one side and TIMESTAMPOFFSET on the other. Choosing the ObjectID as a key gives a warning: rows are then matched by ObjectID, which a copy or reload renumbers.

param.name: compare_fields
param.dialogReference: Fields to compare. Default: every field the two inputs have in common except keys, ObjectID, geometry, GlobalID, BLOB, raster and database-maintained fields such as Shape_Length and Shape_Area. A field is left out when the database maintains it on either side, e.g. when the old data is a shapefile export whose Shape_Area is a plain field and the new data is a geodatabase feature class. When a compare field is a number on one side and text on the other (or a date against either), the run warns: a number and a text are compared by their text form (12 equals "12"), so the type change itself gives no row.

param.name: compare_geometry
param.dialogReference: Compare geometry (default checked). Ignored when either input is a table. Unchecked and without Output Changed Features, geometry is not read at all, so the coordinate systems are not checked (an input with an unknown coordinate system is accepted for an attribute-only diff, and so are a point and a polygon input).

param.name: xy_tolerance_m
param.dialogReference: Geometry moves up to this distance in metres are not reported (default 0.001). Use at least the XY resolution of the data; with 0, a vertex added along a straight edge can be reported as GEOM because of rounding (about 1e-8 m). NaN or infinity is refused. When both inputs have an unknown coordinate system, the value is used in their native units, with a warning, and the report Summary labels it XY tolerance (data units).

param.name: ignore_case_space
param.dialogReference: Compare text without regard to letter case (full Unicode case folding: ß equals ss), leading/trailing spaces and repeated spaces; tabs, line breaks, no-break and other Unicode spaces count as spaces, and composed and decomposed letters (NFC/NFD) match. Zero-width and other invisible characters are kept, so they still make texts differ. Also applies to text keys.

param.name: numeric_tolerance
param.dialogReference: Numbers that differ by no more than this are equal (default 0). With 0, doubles that differ only in the last digits (0.3 and 0.30000000000000004) are reported as changes; the run counts them in a message. Use for example 0.000001 to ignore them. NaN or infinity is refused.

param.name: out_table
param.dialogReference: Output table with one row per change: KEY, CHANGE (ADDED, DELETED, ATTR, GEOM, BOTH, DUP_KEY), FIELD, OLD_VALUE, NEW_VALUE, GEOM_SHIFT (metres), OLD_OID, NEW_OID. OLD_OID and NEW_OID are Long while every ObjectID fits 32 bits; with 64-bit ObjectIDs they are Big Integer in a geodatabase or GeoPackage (an ObjectID beyond 2^53 - 1 is refused before any output is created) and, in a folder, Double while every ObjectID has at most 12 significant digits, else text. ATTR gives one row per changed field. Several key fields are joined with ' | ' in KEY; a text key part that contains '|' (with several key fields), starts with a double quote or is the text <NULL> is put in double quotes, and a date key compared with a text key prints the text it is matched by, so two keys that do not match never print alike.

param.name: out_features
param.dialogReference: Optional feature class with one feature per changed key (the new geometry; the old geometry for DELETED and when the new geometry is null) and one per duplicate-key row. Fields KEY, CHANGE, FIELDS (changed field names), GEOM_SHIFT, OLD_OID, NEW_OID. Requires both inputs to have geometry.

param.name: out_report
param.dialogReference: Optional Excel (.xlsx) report with a Summary sheet (counts per change class, the XY tolerance, the measuring coordinate system and the unit of GEOM_SHIFT) and a Detail sheet (the output table rows). Two CSV files are written instead when .csv is chosen or openpyxl is not available.

tool.usage:
Rows are matched by the key fields, not by ObjectID or position, so inserts and deletes do not shift the comparison. Keys that occur more than once on either side are listed as DUP_KEY and left out of the diff.

Attributes: a null value differs from an empty text; numbers are equal within the numeric tolerance; NaN (not a number) equals NaN and differs from every number (in key fields too: every NaN is one key value, so several NaN keys on one side are DUP_KEY, with a warning); FLOAT (single precision) values are compared as the decimal that was stored (0.1, not 0.10000000149011612); dates are compared exactly (a date-time that carries a UTC offset compares by its instant, and never equals a date-time without an offset: a DATE or DATEONLY field on one side and a TIMESTAMPOFFSET field on the other gives a warning, as a key field every key is then DELETED and ADDED), and a DATEONLY date equals the same day at 00:00 in a DATE field (in key fields too, so a key migrated from DATE to DATEONLY still matches). Geometry: both inputs are read in the same metric coordinate system (the old data's own system if it is projected, otherwise a UTM zone chosen from the data; from the new data when the old data has no coordinates or an unknown coordinate system). An input with an unknown coordinate system (old or new) is refused when the other input has to be projected for measuring (it would be compared in other units) and used as is with a warning otherwise; new data on another datum is projected without a datum transformation, with a warning. When both inputs have an unknown coordinate system, geometry is compared in their native units and the XY tolerance is used as is, with a warning. Lines and polygons that are projected for measuring are first densified in their own system (every 45 m at the default tolerance, at most 100 m), so a straight edge of geographic data is measured as the straight line it is there.

GEOM_SHIFT is the symmetric Hausdorff distance between the old and the new geometry: the largest distance from any point of either one (a vertex or any point along a segment; polygons by their ring boundaries) to the other. The geometry has moved (GEOM) when GEOM_SHIFT is larger than the XY tolerance, and is unchanged otherwise. So a different ring start vertex, ring orientation, part order or line direction, and vertices added or removed along a straight segment, are not changes (with an XY tolerance above 0: at 0, rounding of about 1e-8 m can report such a vertex as GEOM). A line whose only edit is a reversed direction is therefore not reported, which matters for directed lines such as one-way roads or flow lines; a section removed between existing vertices, a gap closed by a new segment, or a ring re-connected along existing vertices is a change, measured at its farthest point. The decision is exact up to a millionth of the XY tolerance (or about 1e-6 m of rounding at UTM coordinates); above the tolerance it is never larger than the true distance and at most max(XY tolerance, 0.1 %) smaller. True curves are densified before comparison. Because polygons are measured by their boundaries, a hole or part that is added or removed counts as its distance to the nearest remaining boundary (removing a 1 m hole in the middle of a 100 m parcel gives about 49 m). A geometry that was added or removed (null on one side) is reported as GEOM with an empty GEOM_SHIFT (0 in a folder output): there is nothing to measure; its changed feature has the old geometry when the new one is null. Geographic data spanning more than 3 UTM zones is measured in the one UTM zone of its centre (with a warning), so shifts far from that zone carry that projection's scale error (GEOM_SHIFT is a distance in the UTM grid, which differs from the distance on the ground by up to about 0.1 % inside a zone). Z and M values are not compared: a change of Z or M alone is reported as unchanged, and Output Changed Features has no Z or M (the run warns when an input has them).

Built-in alternatives: Feature Compare and Table Compare (available at Basic, Esri tool reference) sort both sides by the fields you choose and compare row by row, so after an insert only the first difference is reliable and they give no per-key list of old and new values; this tool fills that capability gap, not a licence gap. Detect Feature Changes is available at Advanced only and compares line features only (Esri tool reference); Pro Change Detector needs the Data Interoperability extension.

Compare fields are found in the new data by name; a field matched otherwise (by alias or a looser name, e.g. STATUS compared with STATUS_CODE whose alias is Status) is reported in a message.

In a folder (dBASE table, shapefile) empty numbers are stored as 0: OLD_OID, NEW_OID and GEOM_SHIFT that do not apply become 0 there, with a warning; write to a file geodatabase to keep them null. A text field there holds at most 254 bytes (UTF-8: an Arabic letter takes 2 bytes, so about 127 Arabic letters); longer texts (KEY, FIELD, OLD_VALUE, NEW_VALUE, FIELDS) are cut to fit and end with ' ...[cut]', with a message (a warning when OLD_VALUE and NEW_VALUE, or two different keys, then read alike); a CSV report keeps the full text, an Excel report up to 32,767 characters per cell. A dBASE table keeps no trailing spaces (the run warns when a written value ends with one), and ArcGIS Pro adds a field Field1 to a dBASE table and Id to a shapefile that are not part of this tool's output. Both output schemas are checked before anything is written or replaced.

Selections and definition queries on layer inputs are honoured. The inputs are never modified. Existing outputs are replaced only when geoprocessing is allowed to overwrite outputs.

Report text: a CSV report puts an apostrophe before text that a spreadsheet would run as a formula (=, @, + or - followed by text, tab, carriage return), so =x is written '=x; an Excel report writes a control character as <U+XXXX> and cuts a cell at 32,767 characters with a visible marker; both show a null value and an empty text alike. The run warns when this makes two different values or keys read the same; the change table always has the exact values.
